newsitem.title: UK: Europe, Brazil dominate as sugar freight origins.
newsitem.headline: Europe, Brazil dominate as sugar freight origins.

text.p: Shipbrokers reported a number of new orders and fixtures on the sugar freight market at the end of the week with European and Brazilian sugars dominating the quoted origins.

Vitol fixed 12/14,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from north Brazil to the Black Sea for end November/early December and Cargill fixed 14,300 tonnes of bagged sugar from Continent to Syria for 20/25 November.
E D & F Man was active on Friday, fixing a number of cargoes and issuing some new inquiries.
It fixed 31,500 tonnes of bulk sugar from Recife and Maceio to Iran plus options, and shipbrokers said the tonnage was booked with Halla. The vessel was 38,000 dwt.
Man also fixed a prompt 22,000-tonne bulk cargo from Paranagua to Morocco, Egypt and Black Sea options.
It quoted for 14,000 tonnes in bags from Veracruz to Colombo for end November/early December and 3,500 tonnes from Gdynia/Gdansk to Thessaloniki and Ploce for prompt shipment.
Sofracom was open for 12,000 tonnes in bulk on its usual run from Reunion to Nantes and was rumoured to have fixed an earlier stem on the same route. Further details have yet to emerge.
